title: InfiniMind: A Learning-Optimized Large-Scale Brain-Computer Interface
problem: Deploying continual learning on NVM-assisted implanted BCI systems incurs excessive write overhead on non-volatile memory, drastically reducing NVM endurance (lifetime) and causing performance bottlenecks that make continual adaptation to non-stationary neural signals impractical.
motivation: Large-scale BCIs require in-device learning to handle signal non-stationarities, but NVM write endurance is severely limited and write latency is high, making naive learning deployment unsustainable for implanted systems.
method: InfiniMind proposes four NVM-write optimization schemes implemented in a memory controller: (1) update filtering exploits sparse and recurring nature of BCI signals to skip unnecessary writes; (2) delta buffering uses temporal locality in neural signals to accumulate deltas and batch NVM writes; (3) out-of-place flushing packs multiple sub-page updates into single page writes to reduce write amplification; and (4) waveform compression exploits structural characteristics of neural waveforms to reduce data volume. These are integrated as a memory controller layer on top of an NVM-assisted BCI system running continual learning algorithms.
key_novelty: A memory controller combining four complementary NVM-write optimizations tailored to the sparse, temporally-local, and structurally-regular characteristics of BCI neural signals.
contributions: Characterization of write overhead patterns in NVM-assisted BCI systems under continual learning workloads.
Update filtering mechanism exploiting BCI signal sparsity and recurrence to eliminate unnecessary NVM writes.
Delta buffering and out-of-place flushing techniques that reduce write amplification using temporal locality.
End-to-end system achieving 5.39x performance improvement and 23.52x lifetime extension over the state-of-the-art NVM-assisted BCI baseline.

metrics.other: 23.52x NVM lifetime extension over state-of-the-art NVM-assisted BCI system

baselines: state-of-the-art NVM-assisted BCI system (without write optimizations)
limitations: Not discussed; applicability beyond stencil-based BCI signal patterns is unclear.
primary_theme: NVM write optimization for continual learning in implanted BCI systems
